images.caption: Palm trees back up the remnants of the old Lanaina fort. The fort was built when sailors from the whaling ships parked off shore shot canons into the town as a protest to the missionary's attempts to clean up their behavior by banning native women from visiting their ships. The fort was built to imprison the rowdy sailors.

images.caption:
Lahaina Banyan Court Park is a public park located at the corner of Front Street and Canal Street in the town of Lahaina, Hawaii, which was the capital of the Kingdom of Hawaii from 1820 to 1845. The 1.94 acres (0.79 ha) park, also known as Lahaina Courthouse Square and commonly called Banyan Tree Park, contains multiple heritage sites on the Lahaina Historic Trail, and a self-guided walking tour through the Lahaina Historic Districts.

The park occupies the site of the Old Lahaina Fort, originally built in 1831. Hoapili, the Royal Governor of Maui, built the fort to protect the town from riotous sailors when Lahaina was used as an anchorage for the North Pacific whaling fleet.
